title: Bundle Up
headline: Cold conditions. Layer up and protect your hands, ears, and face.
quick: Cover your hands, ears, and neck
Warm drinks help you stay comfortable
notification: Cold outside. Layer up before you head out.

wear.top: Thermal base layer, sweater, windproof jacket

do: Warm up indoors before going out
Wear several thin layers, not one thick one
avoid: Cotton next to skin if you sweat
Long exposure without gloves or hat
watchFor: Numb, pale, or waxy fingers and toes

travel: Give the car a minute to warm up
Carry a blanket and phone charger
Leave extra time for your trip
home: Use warm-toned light and hot drinks to feel cozy

people.kids: Dress in layers, keep hands and ears covered, and limit time outside.
people.elderly: Keep the home warm, wear layers indoors, and avoid long outings.
people.pets: Short walks; small and short-haired pets need a coat.
people.commuters: Wear gloves, allow more time, and keep the phone warm.
people.athletes: Longer warm-up; wear layers you can shed.

rules.tip: Near freezing: cover extremities and limit time outside.
Wind chill makes it feel colder. Add a windproof layer.
It gets colder after dark; carry an extra layer.
Damp cold feels sharper. Keep clothes dry.

commonMistakes: Overdressing indoors, then sweating and chilling
Skipping gloves on a short trip
